demos.heading: Restore the shell, pin GIT_SHA, export the runtime settings and prepare the secrets
demos.purpose: Settings back, Python checked, and the commit every image is built from. Run this first in every new terminal. It restores the settings saved in Phases 1 and 2, activates Python 3.12, loads the repository helpers from commands/session-restart.sh and checks Terraform and the Python dependencies. It changes nothing in the cloud. Ends with PASS: shell restored. A Python STOP means rerun S7; a sign-in error means gcloud auth login, and for Terraform also T2. Now pin GIT_SHA: the exact commit every image is built from and every service is deployed with. The first time, it records the commit you have checked out. After that, it checks the checkout still matches. Its form is the short hash, the one the kit's own make build tags images with (GIT_SHA ?= git rev-parse --short HEAD in the Makefile), so a later make deploy-services or make promote finds these images. Never set GIT_SHA by hand to a value that was not built. If you see the “not the checked-out commit” STOP, choose one of the two options it prints; do not mix images from different commits. Check Python syntax in the build inputs: The runtime settings every deploy reads, from Terraform's outputs. Run only after the full reviewed Terraform plan has been applied. A missing or empty output is a stop condition. This block must run in your main shell (not a subshell) because it exports variables for every later step. Rerun it after any restart. The UI's cookie secret and the chat checkpoint DSN. Terraform creates cookie-secret as an empty holder. The UI and admin services mount :latest, so it needs one enabled version. A permission error must be fixed; it is not evidence that no version exists.

demos.heading: Tenants: put people and services on the rosters
demos.purpose: So the UI, MCP and chat accounts go on all three golden tenants (acme, zeta and globex), the A2A agent's account on acme only, and the policies become acme any, zeta any, globex in. The command writes to Firestore with your Application Default Credentials; if it fails with a permission error, run gcloud auth application-default login --no-launch-browser again (Phase 2, T2). Preview first. The dry run writes nothing: Preview first. The dry run writes nothing: Now write it. The command adds members only to the tenant named by --tenant, so put yourself on each tenant in turn. Repeating the service-account entries is harmless: each one is the same Firestore document every time. Each pass prints one ... is on <tenant> line per member and service account, then acme: data_region=any, zeta: data_region=any and globex: data_region=in. Read the rosters back from Firestore, the same documents the API checks on every request: Your email and documind-ui-sa@documind-ai-YOUR-ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com appear under every tenant; documind-agent-sa appears under acme only. To let a colleague in, they need both the door and the list: IAP access on the UI, and a place on the tenant they work in. Add several at once with a comma-separated list.

demos.heading: Finish what make up finishes: the index wait, the managed stores and the BigQuery views
demos.purpose: The kit's own make up does not stop at the deploy. Its recipe names what follows, and this runbook has done most of it by hand: the drift check in T7, the cookie secret in F2, the builds in F3, the deploys in F4 to F8 and the roster in the step before this one: Four remain, and they are the kit's targets, run as they are. wait-index blocks until Firestore's composite indexes leave CREATING. managed-stores switches RAG Engine on once for the project, makes a corpus for each tenant whose text may travel (acme and zeta) and pins acme to rag_engine and zeta to vertex_search, so one deployment answers from all three stores; the data stores themselves were declared by Terraform (managed_search=true). bq-views creates the usage views the admin console reads. vector-status prints the index's own vector count, 0 until the first document is ingested. These targets read the state Phase 2 wrote, because the bucket and prefix are the kit's.
